articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement' (Digest No.109)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement

articleTitle: Error and uncertainty analysis and software facility
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement
abstract: The authors describe the procedures and equations used for calculating uncertainty which are to be published in Edition 2 of NAMAS publication NIS 20. NAMAS is the Government's unified accreditation service for calibration and testing laboratories. The procedures and equations form the basis of a software facility which is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Calculating the uncertainty of a single measurement
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement
abstract: The author discusses methods for evaluating measurement uncertainties and considers both the random uncertainties (Type A) and systematic uncertainties (Type B). A simplified method by which measurement uncertainties can be assessed and safeguards which can be built into the process to monitor the quality of the assessment, are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement
abstract: The author deals with the concept of measurement uncertainty and its standardisation. He describes the ISO/TAG4 Guide method which treats all of the components on a probability basis. He also points out other principal documents produced, namely, WECC 19 by the Western European Calibration Cooperation and the NAMAS NIS 3003.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Uncertainties in Electrical Measurement
abstract: Modern quality systems require that after a suitable time interval (normally referred to as the calibration interval) an instrument is recalibrated, in order to verify that the product still performs to the published warranted specifications (i.e. to assure the continued accuracy of the product). The need to know the 'actual' measured value and the associated uncertainty is discussed and the problem of using the 'significantly out of tolerance' classification is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
